patient.chief_complaint: Confusion and disorientation in a patient with a TIPS shunt
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. H. is a 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis who underwent TIPS (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt) placement 4 months ago for refractory ascites, and has been on rifaximin and lactulose prophylaxis since. His daughter (visiting from out of town) noticed he was confused and disoriented when she arrived, noting he could not remember the day, was repeating himself, and seemed 'out of it.' She was unable to reach him by phone for 3 days before arriving at his apartment. He appeared to have been eating and drinking minimally. His apartment had evidence of diarrhea — his toilet had been used repeatedly with watery stool. His daughter estimated he had 8-10 loose stools per day for the past 3-4 days. He denies alcohol use. He had recently increased his escitalopram dose from 5 mg to 10 mg one month ago.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade II-III), post-TIPS alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) — precipitated by lactulose overdose (8-10 stools/day) causing severe hypokalemia (K 2.6), hypovolemia, and pre-renal AKI; TIPS shunt itself is a structural background contributor.

differential.diagnosis: TIPS shunt malfunction with rebound portal hypertension
differential.key_features: Post-TIPS cirrhotics rely on patent shunt; sudden HE worsening may signal occlusion — assess via Doppler ultrasound.
~25-40% of TIPS patients develop HE within months; this episode is acute-on-chronic.
Escitalopram metabolism is altered in cirrhosis; supratherapeutic accumulation possible but unlikely sole cause.
Paracentesis if any residual ascites; less likely after TIPS but not impossible.
Creatinine 1.6 is mostly pre-renal from hypovolemia; reassess after volume resuscitation.

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive labs: CMP including AST/ALT/bilirubin/INR/albumin, ammonia, CBC, glucose, electrolytes (Na, K, Mg), BUN/Cr, lactate, blood cultures and urine cultures; toxicology if substance use plausible. Confirms liver dysfunction and screens for precipitants.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: K 2.6 (severe hypokalemia), Cr 1.6 (AKI), ammonia 94 — pinpoints over-diuresis from lactulose; cirrhosis features.

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (Post-TIPS HE management; lactulose titration; hypokalemia and HE).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering lactulose dosing, rifaximin, escitalopram in liver disease, diuretics — reduce lactulose dose to target 2-3 stools/day; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.

optimal_actions.action: TIPS Doppler ultrasound — assess shunt patency given new-onset HE worsening.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Interventional radiology assessment of TIPS patency.

optimal_actions.action: Consult hepatology — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.
Early-onset AD genetic panel has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the diagnosis under consideration.
Visual evoked potentials have no role in HE workup; no demyelinating process is on the differential.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: Reduce lactulose dose to target 2-3 soft stools per day — over-titration is iatrogenic.
Aggressive IV potassium repletion (K 2.6 with cardiac monitoring during repletion).
Volume resuscitation with albumin to reverse pre-renal AKI.
Confirm TIPS patency on Doppler ultrasound.
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not interpret lactulose as 'more is better' — the dose target is 2-3 soft stools/day; over-titration is a common iatrogenic HE precipitant.
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Lactulose overdose causes hypovolemia, hypokalemia, and pre-renal AKI — all of which paradoxically worsen HE; titrate to stool frequency, not to ammonia level.
Post-TIPS HE worsening should prompt assessment of shunt patency before assuming a behavioral precipitant.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute HE to escitalopram toxicity / SSRI accumulation.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Escitalopram can have altered metabolism in cirrhosis but is not the primary driver; lactulose overdose with hypokalemia is the dominant precipitant.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Assume TIPS is the cause and request shunt revision; ignore lactulose dosing.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: TIPS is a contributing structural background, but a sudden worsening should prompt patency check AND review of medication titration — lactulose overdose is the proximate cause here.

metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate HE post-TIPS: lactulose overdose causing paradoxical HE via hypokalemia; TIPS shunt patency must be assessed (patent); escitalopram dosing error in liver disease; stool frequency monitoring critical
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 4 required tools + IR consult; iatrogenic precipitant (lactulose overdose) requires recognizing 8-10 stools/day as problematic, not just 'good ammonia control'.
